items.title: Kenanga raises KJTS earnings forecasts on new Thailand cooling contracts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: KJTS Group Bhd's latest cooling contracts in Thailand have prompted Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd (Kenanga IB) to raise its earnings forecasts for the company, citing stronger recurring income from the 20-year agreements. Kenanga IB raised its financial year 2026 (FY26) and FY27 earnings forecasts for KJTS by two per cent and five per cent, respectively, after factoring in four new projects secured by its Thailand unit, KJTN Engineering Co Ltd. The agreements carry fixed fees of about RM48 million over 20 years, equivalent to RM2.4 million in annual recurring revenue, excluding variable fees linked to chilled water consumption.

items.title: Kerjaya Prospek lands maiden data centre job worth RM858mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd's unit Kerjaya Prospek (M) Sdn Bhd has secured an RM858 million contract for fit-out works at a data centre in Johor. The project is targeted for completion within eight months. Kerjaya chief executive officer and executive director Tee Eng Tiong said the award marked an important milestone for the company in the data centre sector.

items.title: Search continues for two more after second teen confirmed drowned in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 3 — The body of one of the three teenagers who went missing while bathing at Tanjung Lompat Beach, Kota Tinggi was found at 1.53 pm today. Tanjung Sedili Zone Maritime headquarters operations officer Lieutenant Commander Mohamed Shafiee Bakar said Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, 16, was found floating about 800 metres from the location where the first victim, Alif Taqiuddin Kamal Hasrul, was found yesterday. He said the victim’s body has been taken for a post-mortem at the Kota Tinggi Hospital.

items.title: Kedah Umno hits back at MoF over KKDW delayed contractor payments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kedah Umno has questioned the Finance Ministry's (MoF) response to Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's remarks on delays in payments to contractors. Kedah Umno information chief Datuk Shaiful Hazizy Zainol Abidin said it is inappropriate for a senior official to publicly respond to the deputy prime minister in such a manner. "Kedah Umno takes the statement by the Treasury secretary-general who claimed that the rural and regional development ministry had spent beyond its allocation seriously.

items.title: Students go behind the scenes of news operations at Media Prima
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: About 20 students from Kolej Profesional Mara Seri Iskandar (KPMSI) today gained first-hand exposure to newsroom and broadcasting operations during a visit to Media Prima Bhd (MPB). The Diploma in English Communication students visited Balai Berita, MPB's headquarters, under Eduscape, an MPB initiative aimed at exposing students to television, radio, print and digital media operations. [[nid:1525001]] Led by News and Current Affairs (NCA) Production Support and Technical Operations manager Abdul Rahim Daim, the tour covered Media Prima Audio, NCA studios, Rev Media Group and the editorial floor of the New Straits Times, Berita Harian and Harian Metro.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia move closer to reopening Tebedu-Entikong trade route
items.summary: JAKARTA: Malaysia and Indonesia are moving closer to reopening trade through the Tebedu-Entikong border route, with the remaining administrative matters expected to be resolved soon. Indonesian Trade Minister Budi Santoso said both countries had agreed on the substantive and regulatory aspects of the border trade issue, with only a few administrative matters remaining. He was met after co-chairing the fourth Malaysia-Indonesia Joint Trade and Investment Committee (JTIC) meeting here on Thursday with Malaysia's Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.

items.title: Tanjung Lompat drowning: Second victim found, search continues for two
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: The second of four victims feared drowned at Pantai Tanjung Lompat, Bandar Penawar, here, was found by the search and rescue (SAR) team at 1.53pm today. Tanjung Sedili Maritime Zone headquarters Operations Officer I Lieutenant Commander Mohamed Shafiee Bakar said the second victim was identified as 16-year-old Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, whose identity was confirmed by his family. "The victim was found floating at a location near where the first victim was found, about 800 metres away," he said at a press conference at the scene here today.

items.title: Indonesia protesters targeted by coordinated disinformation
items.summary: JAKARTA: Disinformation about recent anti-government protests in Indonesia has inundated social media in what researchers say is a coordinated attempt to spread propaganda about the one-year-old movement. "Hoaxes can influence whether someone decides to join a protest or not," said Namora Siahaan, a member of the University of Indonesia Student Executive Board, a group behind similar rallies. Namora cited the spread of false information about protest locations and student arrests, which he said are "likely intended to spread fear and discourage civilians from taking part in the demonstrations."

items.title: Nepal flood toll hits 1,273 as 4,757 remain missing
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Catastrophic floods on the China-Nepal border have killed at least 1,252 people in Nepal, the disaster authority said Thursday, taking overall deaths to more than 1,270. The number of missing in Nepal remained 4,216, as rescue operations continued on a war-footing. In China, state media say there are 541 people missing, taking the overall number to 4,757.

items.title: Law minister: Coroners Bill to be tabled next year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The Coroners Bill, aimed at clarifying the management of death cases, is expected to be tabled in Parliament next year, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. Azalina said drafting the law is expected to establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) and detail the roles of coroners and relevant parties in handling death cases. Azalina said, although procedures for death investigations exist under current legislation, the Coroners Act will complement them and offer clearer guidance on implementation.

items.title: How quickly can Canada pivot?
items.summary: THE resignation of a Prime Minister, one leadership race, a general election, and 23 months later, Canada is now back where it first started: with the Canadian Prime Minister having to reluctantly announce a 'dollar-for-dollar' tariff against its southern neighbour: United States. When Prime Minister Justin Trudeau announced a dollar-for-dollar retaliation in January 2025, he stood alone. When Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the same, starting Sept 8, nearly all Canadian provincial governors expressed support for it.

items.title: Mersing passenger boat detained, crew held for overloading
items.summary: MERSING: A passenger boat carrying 18 people, six over its permitted capacity of 12, was detained by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) off Pulau Besar yesterday. The vessel's 22-year-old skipper and 35-year-old crew member were also detained. Mersing MMEA Maritime Zone deputy operations director Lieutenant Maritime Hazuan Joha said initial checks found the vessel was also operating with insufficient crew.

items.title: China sends third batch of aid to Nepal after flood disaster
items.summary: BEIJING: China has sent a third batch of aid to Nepal after the Aug 26 flooding disaster, including tents, blankets, medical protective suits and satellite communication equipment, the foreign ministry said on Thursday. The China Meteorological Administration and Nepalese meteorological authority have been in contact for video weather consultation and real-time information sharing, and the Tibet region has also provided emergency assistance, the ministry said.--REUTERS PIC © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Oriental Kopi's FMCG gross margin strongest in four quarters – HLIB Research
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd's gross margin for the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) segment in the third quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26) was the strongest in four quarters, said Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB Research). The FMCG segment's gross margin of 44.7 per cent was 8.6 percentage points higher than in the preceding quarter, the research firm noted, and comfortably ahead of the approximately 42 per cent average between the fourth quarter of FY25 and second quarter of FY26. "With a 44.7 per cent gross margin versus 21.5 per cent for café chains, FMCG growth should be structurally margin-accretive at the group level," said HLIB Research in a Sept 3 note, maintaining its outlook with a 'Buy' call and RM1.17 target price.

items.title: Family forced to stay in fire-damaged home after Merdeka blaze
items.summary: Hazwani Zainordin, 39, her husband and their three-year-old son were attending a Merdeka programme at a community hall near their flat in Taman Desa Rakyat Perdana on Aug 23 when they heard cries of "Fire! Fire!" Hazwani said neighbours managed to contain the fire before firefighters arrived and later helped clean up the family's home.

items.title: Tanker safely refloats after running aground near Sungai Johor Bridge
items.summary: Senai-Desaru Expressway Berhad (SDE) said technical inspections found that the bridge structure remained safe and the incident had not affected road users. The concessionaire said the tanker, SMF IXORA, reportedly drifted towards the bridge at about 2.30pm while sailing towards its anchorage amid strong currents and winds. Meanwhile, the Johor Port Authority (LPJ) said the vessel was towed clear of the bridge.

items.title: Azalina: PM term limit and AG/PP separation Bills ready for Parliament
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A Bill to limit the tenure of the prime minister is ready for its second reading in the Dewan Rakyat, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The limit on the prime minister’s term is ready. Azalina said the proposed term limit for the prime minister would involve amendments to the Federal Constitution and would therefore require the support of a two-thirds majority in Parliament.

items.title: Malaysia's foreign worker intake based on industry needs, says Ramanan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has dismissed claims that it plans to recruit 200,000 Bangladeshi workers over the next six months. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said foreign labour intake would be determined by verified industry needs and the ceiling set under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP). He said the figure cited by a Bangladeshi junior minister did not reflect Malaysia's current needs and described the proposed recruitment timeline as illogical.

items.title: 19 Thai undocumented migrants deported
items.summary: BUKIT KAYU HITAM: Malaysia deported 19 Thai illegal immigrants through the Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security Complex here. The Kedah Immigration Department said the group comprised 14 men and five women who had previously been detained at the Belantik Immigration Depot in Sik. They were deported yesterday after completing sentences for offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63 (Act 155) and Immigration Regulations 1963.

items.title: Pas-Umno unity must not be seasonal - Afnan Hamimi
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The unity between Pas and Umno must not be seasonal, appearing only when an election is near and disappearing once it is over, said Pas Youth chief Afnan Hamimi Taib Azamudden. He said both parties needed to build a relationship that transcended political interests and election seasons. "Pas and Umno youth are also working together, serving as a bridge towards greater unity among the ummah.

items.title: Tabung Haji Act amendments in final stages before parliamentary tabling, says TH CEO
items.summary: BANGI, Sept 3 — The process of amending the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) has now reached 90 per cent at the internal level of the Tabung Haji Board (TH) and is expected to be brought to the Cabinet after the technical process and engagement with relevant parties are finalised. TH chief executive officer Mustakim Mohamad said the amendment was among the remaining main actions following the 25 recommendations submitted by the TH Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). The remaining six actions include amendments to Act 535; limiting the scope of Bank Negara Malaysia's supervision of TH and strengthening the disciplinary process.

items.title: Akmal maintains stance to sit out Melaka polls if BN, PH cooperate
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Datuk Dr Muhammad Akmal Saleh has maintained his stance that he will not contest as a candidate if Barisan Nasional decides to cooperate with Pakatan Harapan in the upcoming Melaka election. The Umno Youth chief said he would not compromise his principles for the sake of a position. If BN and PH cooperate, I myself will not contest as a candidate.

items.title: Nearly 90pct of Tabung Haji RCI recommendations near completion
items.summary: BANGI: Nearly 90 per cent of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) recommendations to improve Lembaga Tabung Haji's (TH) internal governance are expected to be completed following amendments to the relevant Act and the institution's regulatory framework. TH chairman Tan Sri Rashid Hussin said most recommendations under the institution's jurisdiction had already been implemented, with the remaining matters requiring cooperation from the government and relevant agencies. "Most recommendations under the institution's internal jurisdiction have already been implemented.

items.title: Families descend on Nepal in search of missing tourists
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Desperate families of missing foreigners were clinging to hope as they combed hospitals and morgues in search of clues, a week after catastrophic floods tore through Nepal's Himalayan border region. Outside Kathmandu's tourist police headquarters, Sanjeev Rai was trapped in agonising uncertainty. "I feel desperate; it's been so many days," he said.

items.title: Kedah RTD seizes lorry with road tax, insurance expired since 1997
items.summary: JERLUN: The Kedah Road Transport Department has seized a lorry found operating with a road tax that expired in 1997 and without valid insurance coverage. He said the 29-year-old driver was also found to be operating without a valid Goods Driving Licence (GDL). "The lorry had been driven to various locations despite having no valid road tax or insurance coverage for 29 years.

items.title: Senior Citizens Bill delayed to early 2027, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 3 — The Senior Citizens Bill, previously targeted for tabling this October, is expected to be brought to Parliament in early 2027. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said that although the draft bill is complete, the process is taking time due to engagement sessions with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and state governments. The new law aims to provide more comprehensive legal protection, particularly in addressing issues of neglect, abuse, and exploitation involving senior citizens.

items.title: Ministry ready to offer psychosocial support to families of Malaysians affected by Nepal disaster
items.summary: Its minister, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, said the ministry is currently awaiting updates from the Foreign Ministry before coordinating any assistance. "We must go through the Foreign Ministry. "We will work together through the Foreign Ministry.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Tech advances require modern laws to combat crime
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the increasingly complex challenges required the government and enforcement agencies to adopt a comprehensive approach involving multiple stakeholders. “Increasingly complex threats require a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Nation approach, bringing together the strengths of the government, enforcement agencies, academia, industry, technology providers and international partners,” he said. Knowledge and research findings must be translated into policies, strengthen enforcement capabilities and produce solutions to the real security challenges faced by the people,” he said.

items.title: Bank Negara maintained OPR on resilient global growth, contained domestic inflation
items.summary: The central bank said the monetary policy stance is consistent with the outlook of continued price stability and sustainable economic growth. However, the MPC will remain vigilant to ongoing developments and assess the balance of risks surrounding the outlook for domestic inflation and growth. "The latest indicators point to resilient global growth, supported by strong global tech expansion, improving supply conditions and stable labour markets.

items.title: Senior Citizens Bill expected in Parliament early 2027, says Nancy
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Senior Citizens Bill, previously targeted for tabling at the October Dewan Rakyat session, is now expected to be brought to Parliament early next year. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the draft bill is complete, but the process has taken longer due to new elements raised during engagement sessions with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and state governments. She said the ministry initially aimed to table the bill this year, but additional amendments required further review.

items.title: Malaysia primed for economic leapfrog, best chance since 1997: Liew
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has its best opportunity since 1997 to leapfrog economically as the post-pandemic shift from efficiency to resilience reshapes global business and investment, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said. He said Malaysia must seize the opportunity by tackling existing challenges, developing solutions and turning them into investable opportunities. Liew highlighted several key challenges and investment opportunities for Malaysia.

items.title: Govt mulls permanent Law Reform Commission
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying a proposal to establish a permanent Law Reform Commission to review national laws and recommend reforms in a systematic, continuous and evidence-based manner. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the proposed commission would serve as a permanent, specialised and structured mechanism to study the country's laws and recommend reforms independently and based on evidence. "The proposal to establish a Law Reform Commission as a permanent, specialised and structured mechanism to study national laws and put forward reform recommendations systematically, continuously, independently and based on evidence.

items.title: Philippines stages school safety drill after shootings
items.summary: BULACAN: As an alarm warning of an active shooter threat blared through a Philippine public school on Thursday, students and teachers moved swiftly into action. The scene at Carlos F. Gonzales High School in Bulacan province was part of a nationwide school safety drill led by the Philippines' Department of Education and its security agencies, as authorities seek to strengthen emergency preparedness following two recent school shooting incidents. A shooting at a high school in the southern Philippines on Aug 18 left two students dead, including the alleged gunman.

items.title: Every reportable death deserves same level of scrutiny, says Azalina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Every death that requires reporting should receive the same level of proper scrutiny, regardless of whether it attracts national attention, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said this was among the principles underpinning the proposed Coroner Bill, which aims to establish a clearer, more independent and transparent framework for investigating deaths and strengthen families' right to know what happened to their loved ones. Perhaps next year would be better," she said.

items.title: FMM pushes for 3pct GST return
items.summary: FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said the previous 6.0 per cent rate had placed a significant burden on businesses and consumers, making a lower 3.0 per cent rate a more reasonable starting point. FMM said a lower-rate GST could help cost pressures and competitiveness challenges faced by manufacturers under the current Sales and Services Tax (SST) system. Another 34 per cent reported higher output costs, 32 per cent cited reduced price competitiveness, and 22 per cent faced cash flow pressures.

items.title: DOE detects STP blower valve fault at manufacturing factory amid Sitiawan river pollution probe
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 3 — The Department of Environment (DOE) has collected industrial effluent samples from a manufacturing factory as part of its investigation into alleged river pollution after fish and crabs were found dead in Sungai Sitiawan. The department said the samples were taken at the premises’ final discharge point to allow investigators to compare them with water samples collected from the river. “Industrial effluent samples were taken at the final discharge point of the premises.

items.title: Three NGO chairmen fined RM600 each for using unauthorised symbols
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Three non-governmental organisation (NGO) chairmen were fined RM600 each after being convicted of using their organisations' symbols without approval from the Registrar. The three were charged at the magistrate's court yesterday under subsection 50(3) of the Societies Act 1966. Deputy Public Prosecutor Lim Zhan Yi led the prosecution.

items.title: Penang gazettes Hungry Ghost Festival as state heritage, six sites also set for official recognition
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 3 — Penang has gazetted the Teong Guan Phor Thor, or Hungry Ghost Festival, as a state heritage item under the Penang State Heritage Enactment 2011, recognising a traditional celebration observed by more than 200 groups across the state. The state also approved the designation of six heritage sites on April 8, Chow said. The earlier list comprised 15 heritage sites, 28 food heritage items and seven intangible heritage items.

items.title: Court of Appeal sets aside fraud, conspiracy findings in RM52.2m Johor land dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The Court of Appeal has set aside findings of fraud and conspiracy against a businessman and property agent in a dispute over a proposed RM52.2 million sale of a 22ha tract of land in Johor. However, a three-member panel upheld the High Court’s findings that no binding sale agreement had been concluded and that businessman J. Siva Kumar had wrongfully lodged a private caveat over the land. Siva and Ammsa had sought specific performance of an alleged sale and purchase agreement with Firwas.

items.title: SAR area expanded to two nautical miles in search for three missing teenagers in Tanjung Lompat
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 3 — The search and rescue (SAR) operation for three teenagers missing at Tanjung Lompat in Bandar Penawar has been expanded to cover up to two nautical miles of coastal waters today. Tanjung Sedili Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) acting director Mohd Najib Sam said the search area was widened following the discovery of one victim about 500 metres from the incident site yesterday. “Today’s SAR operational area has been increased from one to two nautical miles of coastal area in an effort to locate the three missing teenagers.

items.title: Asyraf Wajdi says only Zahid can decide whether he should step down as Mara chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Mara chairman Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki today said only Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi could decide whether he should step down from the position. “I was appointed by the Deputy Prime Minister, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister. Asyraf said Mara’s reputation and role as a Malay and Bumiputera institution must be protected from efforts to undermine it.

items.title: Umno’s future direction, unity govt ties among key issues at upcoming general assembly, says Asyraf Wajdi
items.summary: Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said political cooperation, particularly within the framework of the unity government, and the Rumah Bangsa agenda proposed at the previous Umno General Assembly were the two most popular issues raised by the divisions. “The main motions include the issue of Umno’s direction and political cooperation, particularly within the framework of the unity government, as well as the Rumah Bangsa agenda proposed at the previous Umno General Assembly. Asyraf also said 6,401 delegates would attend this year’s Umno General Assembly.

items.title: Penang eyes record manufacturing investments after RM17.3b secured in first half
items.summary: “Penang’s RM17.3 billion in approved manufacturing investments from January to June represented a 38 per cent increase from the corresponding period last year,” he said. The figure accounted for 34 per cent of Malaysia’s total approved manufacturing investments, he said. Expansion projects made up RM11.9 billion, or 69 per cent, of the total approved investments, while new projects accounted for RM5.4 billion, he said.

items.title: Sultan Ibrahim meets Singapore FM at Istana Pasir Pelangi in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 3 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today granted an audience to Singaporean Foreign Affairs Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan today. According to Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook post, the audience took place at Pavilion 2 of Istana Pasir Pelangi Polo Grounds, here. Also present were Singapore’s High Commissioner to Malaysia Vanu Gopala Menon and Consul-General in Johor Bahru Ng Kuan Hai.

items.title: Zairil accuses Hadi of using religious sentiment to deflect Tabung Haji scrutiny
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 3 — Penang DAP vice-chairman Zairil Khir Johari today accused PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang of using religious sentiment to divert attention from alleged governance and integrity failures at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Zairil said Hadi’s alleged description of the issue as an “attack on Islamic identity” was an attempt to deflect scrutiny from the institution’s management. He also questioned Hadi’s silence when alleged wrongdoing at TH was disclosed through the Royal Commission of Inquiry report last month.

items.title: ‘Malaysia, Jom Check!’: Free health screenings for STR recipients aged 40 and up
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — ProtectHealth Corporation Sdn Bhd (ProtectHealth) under the Ministry of Health (MOH) is offering free health screening services to eligible Malaysians through the PeKa B40 2026 Programme in conjunction with the ‘Malaysia, Jom Check!’ ProtectHealth in a statement today announced that the community health screening programme nationwide on Sept 5 to 6 aims to provide Malaysians with an opportunity to check their health status. According to ProtectHealth, the PeKa B40 2026 Programme is also being implemented to encourage the public to undergo regular health screenings to detect high blood pressure, diabetes and high cholesterol problems at an early stage before they become more serious.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji COO’s corruption charges postponed after hospitalisation
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 3 — The reading of corruption charges against former Lembaga Tabung Haji chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani, who was scheduled to be charged today, was postponed after he was hospitalised for a heart problem. Adi Azuan, 56, was initially scheduled to appear before the Sessions Court here to face several charges under Section 165 of the Penal Code. When the case was called this morning, his lawyer Wan Azman Aiman Wan Fakhruddin informed Sessions Court judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud that his client had been hospitalised since Aug 31.

items.title: TH Properties unit ex-manager hit with three CBT charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A former Health and Safety Manager of THP Bina Sdn Bhd was charged in the Sessions Court here today with three counts of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM72,000 in penalty funds collected in connection with a proposed office complex development project in Putrajaya. THP Bina is a wholly owned subsidiary of TH Properties Sdn Bhd, which in turn is a subsidiary of Lembaga Tabung Haji. The penalty funds were related to a proposed office complex development in Precinct 3, Putrajaya, comprising: PT 12081 (Block A – 10-storey office, Block B – 9-storey office, an auditorium, and three levels of basement parking); PT 12075 (Block C – 7-storey office and two levels of basement parking); and PT 12074 (Block D – 9-storey office and two levels of basement parking).

items.title: Haze drives up demand for bottled water, health products in Kuching
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 3 — The haze has driven up demand for bottled water and health-related products at supermarkets here, with some retailers increasing their stock levels to meet customer needs. At Farley Kuching, drinks department supervisor Nelson Ting, 23, said bottled water was selling faster than usual since the haze began. Despite the increase in demand, Ting said the supermarket had not experienced any shortage of bottled water so far.

items.title: PAS Youth wants party to defend all existing seats in future elections
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 3 — PAS Youth has passed a motion calling for the party to defend all its existing parliamentary and state seats in future elections, including when it cooperates with other parties, Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported. PAS Youth information chief Khairul Nadzir Helmi Azhar said the motion, tabled by a Padang Terap delegate, was unanimously approved by more than 800 delegates at the wing’s annual muktamar. He said it was among six motions approved by PAS Youth to be brought to the main PAS muktamar, which begins today.

items.title: Two plastic waste warehouses destroyed in Shah Alam fire, premises had no fire safety system
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 3 — Two warehouses processing plastic waste were destroyed in a fire in Section 32 here last night, with three forklifts, a lorry and two compressors also caught in the blaze, Sinar Harian reported. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar was quoted as saying the department received an emergency call about the incident at 10.59pm. He said 26 personnel and officers from the Shah Alam Fire and Rescue Station, assisted by teams from the Andalas, Bukit Jelutong and North Klang stations, were sent to the scene with fire engines.

items.title: Rural Development Ministry wants RM4b for road projects, says already used 94pc of 2026’s RM2b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) estimates that it requires about RM4 billion annually to ensure the continued implementation of ongoing rural road projects and newly approved ones. For 2026, rural road projects were allocated RM2.107 billion, with 415 projects implemented as of Sept 1, involving expenditure of about RM1.995 billion, or 94 per cent of the allocation, it said. KKDW said rural road development was not merely about implementing physical infrastructure projects, as good road connectivity had a direct impact on the daily lives of rural communities.

items.title: Kuching banker gets seven years’ jail, 16 lashes after draining client accounts via DuitNow
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 3 — A relationship manager with an international bank was yesterday sentenced to seven years’ jail, fined RM40 million and ordered to receive 16 strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court here after pleading guilty to fraud and money laundering charges. For each of the eight money laundering charges, he was sentenced to three years’ jail, with the terms to run concurrently from today, fined RM5 million or four months’ jail in default. Kho failed to pay the fine.

items.title: Victoria Bridge incident: Father speaks on losing youngest son a year after eldest daughter
items.summary: The victim’s father, who wished to be known only as Abd Halim, 42, said his eldest daughter was only 16 when she died last year, following a four-month battle with an illness doctors were unable to diagnose. He said the family was still coping with the loss of their eldest daughter when tragedy struck again with the death of Abdul Rafee, three. “Just last year, we lost our eldest child.

items.title: SDEB refutes viral claims of Sungai Johor Bridge closure, says safe to cross despite vessel strike
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept — The Sungai Johor Bridge here is safe for all road users, according to Senai-Desaru Expressway Berhad (SDEB). In a statement, SDEB said it had taken immediate action by conducting inspections and assessments of the bridge’s structural condition, following the incident of a vessel that drifted close to the bridge around 2.30 pm yesterday. SDEB said that it always prioritises safety aspects and will continue to monitor the condition of the bridge structure from time to time to ensure the safety of highway users.

items.title: Mercy Malaysia deploys team to Nepal as 2.2 million tonnes of debris hamper aid to flood-hit communities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Mercy Malaysia has deployed a humanitarian team to Nepal to assess urgent needs following the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Bhote Koshi river system on Aug 26, with the team set to focus on search and rescue, emergency shelter, food, clean water and sanitation as millions of tonnes of debris hamper access to affected communities. Mercy Malaysia said its team will assess the situation on the ground, engage with affected communities and local partners, and identify the most urgent humanitarian needs. Roads and bridges have been destroyed or blocked by massive quantities of debris, making access to affected communities increasingly difficult.

items.title: DOE steps up patrols amid worsening haze crisis, warns landowners against open burning
items.summary: Elaborating further, Rosli said that motor vehicle movements also generally contribute to the decline in air quality. A total of 16 stations recorded unhealthy API readings, with Bintulu, Sarawak recording the highest at 192, followed by Kapit, Sarawak (190), Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic, Sabah (178), Keningau, Sabah (175), and Kota Kinabalu, Sabah (173). Also recording unhealthy readings were Labuan (173), Samalaju, Sarawak (172), Kimanis, Sabah (171), ILP Miri, Sarawak (170), Limbang, Sarawak (169), Miri, Sarawak (166), Johan Setia, Selangor (159), Putrajaya (151), Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (151), Sandakan, Sabah (136), and Seremban, Negeri Sembilan (109).

items.title: BUDI95 fuel quota back to 300 litres: How will this affect motorists?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Five months after reducing the monthly subsidised RON95 quota from 300 litres to 200 litres, the government has restored the higher limit. But with government data showing average monthly RON95 consumption is around 100 litres, what does the restored litres mean for current consumers? A motorist who uses 100 litres a month will still purchase only 100 litres.

items.title: Second suspect arrested after Sri Petaling cable‑theft chase; remanded seven days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Police have detained another local man to assist in investigations into a cable theft case in Sri Petaling here. Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the 32-year-old man was believed to be the driver of a Ford Ranger which was pursued on Monday from the Awan Besar Toll Plaza heading towards Klang (West) before the chase ended at Jalan Hang Tuah 4. On Monday, a police team fired several shots before detaining a 29-year-old man suspected of cable theft after the Ford Ranger driven by his accomplice attempted to flee a police inspection in Sri Petaling.

items.title: Sunway Lagoon says all injured guests discharged, keeps roller coaster closed pending probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The roller coaster attraction involved in the August 22, 2026 incident at Sunway Lagoon theme park in Subang Jaya, which is believed to have stopped abruptly after failing to move forward during a ride, remains closed while investigations are ongoing. “Sunway Theme Parks remains firmly committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety and to ensuring the well-being of everyone who visits our parks,” it said. Sunway Theme Parks confirms that all guests who were admitted to the hospital for further observation following the incident have now been discharged.
